utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Pantelic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We discussed a few documents yesterday, and we need to discuss a few more today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's a decision of the executive board, dated 11th of October, 1992. It's a decision on the transportation for the work assignment, on the transport of persons who have compulsory work obligation assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I ask for the reference number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your reference number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The reference number is IO5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, could you please tell me who -- first of all, are you familiar with this document, and could you please tell me what the basis was for this decision by the executive council.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember this decision. The Crisis Staff reached a decision to introduce a regular bus line and tasked the executive council to work out this issue, and we adopted a decision that all persons who had a work assignment could use public transport in the town, including the buses of the companies who were allowed to operate, and they didn't have to pay for this service. My duty was to make a contract with this company in order to compensate them for the transport services for the current month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this decision to include all the people who were under work obligation, or were there any differences there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All people, regardless of their ethnicity, used the free bus transport from their place of work to their place of residence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long this decision was in effect. Was it only during 1992, or did it also apply in subsequent years?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in effect for quite a long time. In fact, throughout the entire war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have an exhibit number, if there is no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be Exhibit D114/1 and D114/1 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document that I would like to discuss with the witness is -- our internal number is IO6. It's a decision issued by the executive board -- municipal executive board on the 20th of November, 1992. I believe the decision is related to the conditions regarding the economy and relations between economy subjects in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, could you please tell me what you know about this decision or this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Secretariat for the Economy monitored the work of the economic subjects, i.e., the socially-owned enterprises and then in the month of November came out with a proposal to begin to carry out a decentralisation in terms of the operation and management of the socially-owned enterprises. So this decision is -- its purpose is to make it possible to make the conditions of work much better, and here it is stated what is necessary to be done in the forthcoming period in order to carry out this decentralisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please, Ms. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D115/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is IO7. This is a letter signed by the vice-president of the executive board, dated 27th of November, 1992. It's a request for approval of the telephone lines between Modrica and Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, can you please tell me something about this document, excuse me. I just want to interrupt you for a second. I assume that you have signed it, because I see your first and last name at the bottom of the document.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I signed it. And the document is as follows: On the 20th or the 21st of April, 1992 our telephones were cut off -- or let's say it better. The receiver in Gradacac was disrupted, which was under the control of the Muslims, so that our receiver could not receive signals through that receiver, and for that reason all the telephone connections in the municipality were cut, and we were cut off from the rest of the world. On that occasion, we tried through the railway company to resolve at least the question of several telephone numbers, since the railway company had its own telephone lines which were dug under the ground and they had a special system and a special network. So I asked them to make five phone numbers available to us, which we would distribute in various institutions throughout the territory of the municipality. So this request pertains to this matter that I've just talked about.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibits D116/1 and D116/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My next document that I would like to discuss with this witness is -- is the -- the reference is IO8. This is a conclusion or decision issued by the executive board on the 21st of December, 1992, with regard to the health situation with the haemodialysis centre and health issues in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The copy is terrible -- at least, the one that I have -- and I don't think that yours is any better. But if you can recall, please tell us what did this decision pertain to. Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I commented on the report from the business trip of the chief of the haemodialysis department of the hospital and the head of the Red Cross, and this is the conclusion in accordance with which they went to Belgrade and Vrsac so ask for assistance regarding the kidney machines, or also medicines that are used in haemodialysis. So this was a request sent to Yugoslav doctors, to Doctors Without Borders, and also to the medicines factory Hemofarm in Vrsac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibits D117/1 and D117/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is with reference IO9. This is a decision issued by the executive -- municipal executive board on the 24th of December, 1992, a decision on the establishment of a subcommission for the reception and temporary accommodation of refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, you already talked about the problems because of the number of the refugees and also the general situation in Samac, so I'm asking you, please, to comment briefly on this decision, if you know what the basis was for this decision and if you know what its purpose was.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government of Republika Srpska passed a law on refugees, and under the regulations of that law a republican commission was formed to receive and accommodate those refugees. Then it was necessary in the municipalities to form municipal subcommissions which would together with the republican commission work on the resettlement of those refugees, and this decision talks about how these persons as representatives of the municipality were obliged in coordination with the republican commission for refugees to work to receive and settle those refugees in the territory of the municipality. So this pertained to all the persons, all the refugees who came to our municipality and were sent to our municipality by the republican commission for refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even though you know the composition of this commission and that the people who were on the commission had specific professions, could you please tell us something about that. Who were the people in the committee -- commission? What was their profession? And did that have any significance in relation to the accommodation of the refugees? Briefly.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you first this: This committee was a multinational one. The composition of the members of the committee was determined by those who were supposed to come to our municipality. So these were workers from the centres for social work, commissioner for refugees, a physician, and representatives of the executive council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibits D118/1 and D118/1 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Another document is reference IO10. This is a letter signed by the executive board and sent to the -- to the telephone and post company, dated 14th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've already spoken about the problems that existed with telephone lines. I assume that this memo, although it dates from 1993, is linked to the previous memo that we've looked at and is also directed at resolving the same problem with telephone lines. So just briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous memo from 1992 was not sufficient for us to solve the problem with telephone lines. Now, this new memo we sent in order to request the socially-owned companies from Republika Srpska to do their utmost to install the equipment which would link the entire municipality through telephone connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibits D119/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following document - and I think that's the last document from this set of documents - [In English] The reference number is IO11. This is a conclusion of the executive board -- the municipal executive board with regard to the trade enterprises in the area of the municipality, dated 28th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is another operational document similar to those that were discharged on a daily level. But just give us a few comments regarding it.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document stemmed from the work programme of the municipal assembly for 1993. The Secretariat for Economy was tasked with creating information on the quality and level of supplies of consumer goods in our municipality. The Secretariat for Economy was supposed to do this in cooperation with the Secretary for Commerce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibits D120/1 and ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, we have completed the analysis of a small part of documents that the Defence has prepared as part of its case in order to illustrate to the Trial Chamber the way the municipality and its organs functioned. This was just a small fragment of their total work. I would like now to ask you for your opinion, for your position regarding the description of the work of administrative municipal organs from April 1992 until late 1993. We heard from you a lot of comments that were given with respect to various documents, but could you summarise that for us and give us your conclusion. What was the work of municipal organs like in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will attempt to contain my answer in just a few sentences. Let me start by saying that in 1992 the executive council did not work with full membership. It had to work in extremely difficult conditions with a backlog of problems. The intense shelling of the town and surrounding villages, due to the fact that our municipality is stretched along the front lines, either with the Croatian or the Muslim side, is something that created problems in addition to the problems that existed with engaging people to perform their work obligation, ensuring that the military consented to people being exempted from the military service in order to serve their work obligation. On top of all that, we had a problem with a large influx of displaced persons and refugees that came into our municipality during 1992, but those municipal employees and members of the executive council that worked during 1992 have done their utmost to meet the obligations of the executive council and to ensure that every citizen that applied to the executive council or to relevant agencies encountered understanding on their part and received a reply that was requested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the work of the municipal administration, were there any cases of ethnic discrimination? Were some ethnic groups favoured or were these efforts made by employees and members of the executive council directed to all residents, irrespective of their ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In administration organs, those who worked there were professionals, those who worked in the administration even prior to the eruption of the conflict. And all three ethnic groups were represented among them. The number of Serbs was greater, however. There was Croats and Muslims in the administration as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, this now: The activity of the municipal administration aimed at resolving the problems that the population encountered, was it selective in view of certain ethnic groups or was it driven by the desire to provide everything that all residents in Samac municipality needed?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's three leading questions, and very loaded leading questions in that question my learned friend was putting to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, the objection is sustained. Can you reorganise your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, what is your personal belief and your personal knowledge regarding the aim, the purpose of the efforts made by the municipal administration?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no discrimination whatsoever. The interests of everyone were protected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But regardless of all of your efforts, in Samac, due to the state of war and the situation that existed, certain incidents broke out. Now, please tell me, what do you know about a certain number of volunteers that came to the territory of Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that I first heard that they had arrived. That was sometime in late April. Yes -- oh, no, rather, early April. I saw some of them in the street in passing; however, I didn't have any contact with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout 1992, did municipal organs have contacts with a certain number of those volunteers under some circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information regarding that. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those first few months, did they come to the building where the executive municipal organs were housed? How did they behave? Do you have any knowledge regarding this?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of May or June I noticed on several occasions that Dragan Djurdjevic came to see Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, have you heard about the incident which took place in Crkvina in the first half of May of 1992 whereby Lugar killed a certain number of non-Serb residents of Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I have heard about that. That was on the following day. I received this information from the chief of police, Savo Cancarevic. And let me just tell you that I had goose bumps all over me. Both of us were horrified as he was telling me this story.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Here in the transcript we have, "I received this information from the chief of police, Savo Cancarevic." It's line 11 -- it's page 11, line 1 and 2. We used these words "chief of police" for Mr. Stevan Todorovic. He said actually, "the commander of the police." Because -- just not to have something in the transcript that would -- that may cause maybe some misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, what was the official post of Mr. Savo Cancarevic, whom you've mentioned in your previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Savo Cancarevic was the commander of the police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Just for the sake of clarify right now, then, could Mr. Lukic tell us what is the difference between the chief of police and the commander of the police, just to have it on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain this to Her Honour Williams.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police organisation looks like this: Minister of the Interior, Minister of Police, head of the public security centre, and then within that public security centre there is a number of police stations, and then below that is the Public Security Station. At the head of the Public Security Station is a chief of the Public Security Station, and then within the station itself there are several departments: Police, criminal investigation department, general department, department for traffic, licences and traffic, and the financial department. At the helm of all of these departments is the chief of police, and one of the departments is headed by the commander of police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you. So I take it from your answer, then, that Mr. Stevan Todorovic was senior to Mr. Savo Cancarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, on that occasion did Savo Cancarevic or somebody else tell you what legal steps would be taken or who would be in charge of the investigation? Did he tell you this then or perhaps at a later time? Just tell us what you know.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I naturally asked him who was the perpetrator of that crime, and he told me that it was Lugar and that the investigation had been launched and was ongoing, which meant that I shouldn't put any more questions to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In mid-May and further on in 1992 and in 1993, did the Croat residents of Samac -- were they ever forcibly placed at vital facilities in town?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you lived in Samac as a citizen and held an office there, please tell me, what do you personally know about certain incidents and crimes committed by Stevan Todorovic? First of all, do you know whether he committed anything of this nature?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that at that time I heard, also from Savo Cancarevic, that Stevan killed a man and that they were conducting an inquiry at the centre for public security regarding the circumstances of that event. But until I saw a published indictment or until I talked to persons who returned after 1996 to town, I didn't really know much about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you describe the relationship between Blagoje Simic and Stevan Todorovic in that period, 1993, if possible? How did you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1992, from the 17th of April, 1992 and until the end of 1992, I didn't see either one of those men very often, but I heard that their relationship wasn't really great and that there were some conflicts in the work of each man. I heard that from Milan Simic, the president of the executive council.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask for the witness again to repeat the date. Was it 1992 or 1993 that the question pertained to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since in my question -- [In English] Yes. My question was the period from April 1992 until the end of 1993. [Interpretation] So I asked you about this period, because of the transcript -- we were talking about the period from April of 1992 to the end of 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the relationship of Stevan Todorovic with other municipal officials from other services? Do you have any details or any particular information regarding his conduct that you can tell us about? Was he a man who was a cooperative man or --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of 1992, he didn't come to the executive council, but I did see that he visited Milan Simic. I did see him in his office quite often. But as far as I know, other members of the executive council didn't socialise or didn't have many meetings with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you're a lawyer from the legal profession, could you please tell me who is in charge of conducting criminal investigations. Who was in charge in the period of April 1992 to the end of 1993, since that is the period covered by the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police and the civilian prosecutor, if we're talking about civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other category? What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they were members of the military, then that was under the jurisdiction of the military prosecutor and the military court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since your office was in the municipal building which is on the banks of the river Sava and since the TO building is across the street from that building, did you ever hear any kind of cries or moaning or did you hear any sounds of beatings from the TO? If you heard anything, tell us. And if not, just say so.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that the municipal building is about 15 or 20 metres away from the edge of the TO building, the side of the TO building, and I did not hear any cries, but I often did hear singing from the TO headquarters building and I heard that several persons were singing the same song. After work hours I lived in a village which was 11 kilometres away from town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you heard the same song being sung a few times. Did you recognise the song? Would you be able to tell us what type of song it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can say that they were singing Serbian songs, those songs that were usually sung by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could this song be heard -- could this singing also be heard from the heating plant?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you repeat your question. I didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, could you hear that singing also from the heating plant building and how far was that heating plant away from the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that it could be heard, because the heating plant is about 2 kilometres away from the municipal building, if not more. It's at the other end of town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you determine the time period when you heard this singing? Was this over the next several months? Was that during the entire 1992? Was it during 1993? Could you please give us some kind of time frame about that.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in the course of 1992, and I cannot remember that it happened again subsequently, that it was ever heard afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your knowledge about the detained persons in Samac? Were there any such persons? How many of them, if you know? Where were they detained and on what grounds?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I didn't have any contacts with Stevan Todorovic, I was interested not as a person who was responsible but as a citizen, since I was performing completely different kind of work. So I was interested to know what kind of people were there at the TO building, the TO headquarters. I had this conversation with Savo Cancarevic, since he used to stop by my office frequently requesting cigarettes for the police or tins of food for policemen, since they had to go out to the line. And then he told me that in the TO headquarters building and in the secondary school, in the high school there were certain persons who were under investigation, certain investigative procedures were being conducted about those people, and they were the ones who were carrying out these operative inquiries or tasks. And as far as the number is concerned, he said that the figure was around 300 persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find out from him or from someone else what these people were suspected of doing?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told me on that occasion that there were indications that some of those people were preparing an armed rebellion, that weapons were found on some of those people, military weapons, and that the investigative proceedings were being carried out at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, could you please tell me the following: What is your personal opinion on the following. Was there any kind of plan in the work of the municipal bodies in that period to jeopardise human rights of the non-Serb population in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness's opinion is irrelevant. The Trial Chamber should be interested in facts, what he knew as opposed to his opinion on this particular matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the work of your municipal administration and the town administration, did you ever discuss or adopt any decisions which were aimed at jeopardising the human rights of non-Serb citizens in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No further questions for this witness, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other counsel from the Defence? Mr. Lukic -- oh, I'm sorry, the Judge has a question first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Yes. I -- the day before yesterday I asked you -- you presented a document signed RH27, and you said that you will come back to it later on. You haven't done so, so I ask you whether you are tendering it into evidence or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that we have discussed yesterday. Could you just read me the title of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: "Decision on the working hours of administration organs, economic and other," and so on. But you haven't referred to this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have -- I have -- I have information that we tendered that into evidence yesterday, and also just now the witness confirmed that. Maybe we could -- we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: It hasn't any number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we verify with the registry, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document was admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: On the 26th of November. And it is now Exhibit D97/1 and D97/1 ter for the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: D97. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination -- oh, I'm sorry, Mr. Lukic Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Lukic. Lukic questioning Lukic. I hope there won't be any problems if the Trial Chamber addresses either one of us and that there will be no mistake. Mr. Lukic, my first question is: How long have you known Miroslav Tadic? And I represent Mr. Tadic. How long have you known him? Did you know him before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly, but I've known him for quite a long time now. Since I was the director of the Internal Revenue Agency and he had a restaurant, if nothing else we knew each other for business reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We've heard from your testimony so far about your activities in the political structures and in the pre-war government structures. And when I say "before the conflict," I mean before the outbreak of the conflict in April 1992. Do you know if Miroslav Tadic was a member of any political party during the war and before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any information about his political activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Miroslav Tadic on any occasion at meetings of the pre-war government structure?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the meetings that I attended, I never saw him there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to submit a new document. For my friends from the Prosecution, it's a document with internal mark PD110/3 -- PDB110/3. A copy has already been provided to my learned friends, and I would ask the usher to provide a copy for the Trial Chamber and for the registry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a decision by the executive council of the municipality of Samac from the 22nd of May, 1993 about the naming or appointment of a commission for the exchange of captured and other persons. Mr. Lukic, the signature is not legible here, but I would like to ask you if you are familiar with this document and if you remember signing it.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is from the executive committee, and I do not doubt that it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about this document? What was its purpose and what was the relationship of this commission to the executive council?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that the workers of the Red Cross turned up with a proposal that there was a number of persons from our municipality who wished to leave our municipality and that it was necessary to issue a decision to form a commission or a committee which would officially perform this task. And then I issued instructions for a draft proposal to be prepared for the executive council, which the service did. And this decision was adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown document P83 and for this document to remain in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please take a look at this document. It is dated in October. It has a very similar content, but there are also certain differences. Do you know that before you passed this decision the committee was accountable for its work to the War Presidency? Do you know something about that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew that this committee was established by the War Presidency and that this committee existed and performed its work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the executive council passed this decision in May, did the committee occasionally inform the executive council on its work, as is mentioned in paragraph 3? And if so, how often did they do so?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that they did inform us. And as to how often, I really couldn't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that Miroslav Tadic came or perhaps Velja [as interpreted] Maslic or perhaps another person?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was Velimir Maslic who informed the executive council on behalf of the committee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if there are no objections, I would like to have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's no objection to the document Mr. Lukic has provided to the Prosecution, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D76/3 and D76/3 ter for the B/C/S version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following document I would like to discuss with you touches upon the topic that had already been discussed by this witness, and it has an internal -- the internal number of PDB47/3. It had been delivered to the OTP. And this is a request to issue receipt for firewood, and it's dated 29th August 1992. Mr. Lukic, yesterday you told us about the decision of the executive council establishing criteria for distribution of firewood. I would like you now to comment on this document. What was the procedure applied with respect to persons that applied to the municipality to receive firewood? And could you also tell us whether you knew this particular family that is mentioned in this document and what was the ethnic background of this person that petitioned the executive council?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I commented on the decision of the executive council and the decree of the government concerning the supply of firewood for the coming winter. The petitioner here is of a Muslim ethnicity, whereas her husband is a Croat. At least judging by the first and last name I can conclude that the husband is a Croat. She, just like everybody else, sent a petition, and it is stated here that a truckload of firewood and 2 tonnes of coal were allotted to her. That means that her petition was granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the OTP has no objections, I would like to have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see none. Yes. Let's have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D77/3 and D77/3 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to analyse another document with an internal marking of PDB68/3. This is a request to compensate for the expenses for purchasing medicine, and this document is dated 11th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, can you please explain this document to us, if you have any personal knowledge regarding this. Also, could you tell us something about this issue and the attitude that the executive council had with respect to matters mentioned in this request.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that there were a lot of requests of this nature and similar ones. This document deals with some rare medications that were not easy to come by. We, or rather, the executive council granted requests of this nature, and in the course of 1993 and 1994 we established and made operational a humanitarian pharmacy where people similar to this petitioner were able to receive medications free of charge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, please, this petitioner here, Barjaktarevic Hikmeta, could you tell me what you know about the ethnicity of this petitioner.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The petitioner is of a Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could this document please be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D78/3 and D78/3 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would just like you to comment on the document that had already been discussed and admitted here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown document D63/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document has just one page, and I would like you to read it carefully, Mr. Lukic. Could you comment on this document, please. Yesterday you mentioned apartments, but I would like you to focus on the attitude that the civilian protection staff within the executive council had with respect to these matters.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that one of the activities of the civilian protection staff was to register all temporarily abandoned apartments and houses and to seal them. Here they wrote up a memo and informed us about the measures that had been taken on the 14th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please: This person regarding whom the civilian protection staff informed the executive council that temporary housing was found for them, do you know these three families and do you know perhaps where were their houses located in relation to the front line? If you know, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know these individuals. Their houses were right next to the Sava banks, near the delta of the Bosna River, and their houses had been destroyed by shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person listed under number 1, Tokalic Mujo, what do you know about his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that on the list of vacant houses and apartments there were a lot of Serb houses in view of what transpired in May?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know. Two of me relatives were on that list, and there were a lot of similar cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the civilian protection staff upon providing this list have anything to do with allocation of these apartments?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't do anything else after that. Yesterday I told you that a committee had been established which took decisions to the housing facilities and made records on temporary award of these houses and apartments to the homeless people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions regarding this document, but I would like to ask you something about a matter that I'm interested in. Do you have any information about the executive organ -- executive council or any other organ passing a decision making it mandatory for non-Serb residents to wear a white armband?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The executive council certainly didn't pass such a decision, and I don't know of any other organ passing that kind of a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have finished my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Any --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence of Mr. Zaric does not wish to examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Cross-examination by the Prosecution. Cross-examined by Mr. Re:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you just said you knew of no order for people to wear white armbands. Did you ever see people wearing white armbands in the streets of Bosanski Samac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that people were wearing -- non-Serbs, that is, Croats and Muslims, were wearing white armbands in the streets of Bosanski Samac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- before I go further, I just want to clear up a few things. Were you the Captain Mirko Lukic who was a captain in the army reserve in Bosanski Samac Municipality in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during 1992, were you living -- or 1993, were you living in Ulica Ivo Lola Ribar in the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have an apartment there; however, I lived in Gornja Slatina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what number is your apartment in that street?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: S17, number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you owned the apartment there for?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since 1976.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You owned it in 1992, then. Were you staying in it during the time you were the vice-president of the executive council of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is not actually an objection, but I don't see if this question is quite proper, because our learned colleague said "you owned it in 1992." First of all, maybe our colleague was not here from the beginning of the trial, so there were differences between ownership of the apartment, tenancy of the apartment. So maybe it will be better to ask first if he actually was the owner of the apartment or he had just a tenancy contract in respect of this apartment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure the way the question was put, the witness was going to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I asked him whether he owned it and he said he owned it since 1976. He didn't say he was a tenant or had social ownership occupancy rights or anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, he says I have an apartment there, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was a tenant because at the time apartments were not privately owned. I had a tenancy right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whatever. You had an apartment in that street in 1992; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had the rights to use, occupy, and -- sorry, and use that apartment during 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And occasionally I would use it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's during the period when you were the vice chairman or the chairman of the executive council of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of 1992, the apartment was shelled and damaged; therefore, during that time, until the apartment was repaired, I was unable to live there, and this lasted for some two months. I would occasionally stay in the apartment, both when I was vice-president of the executive council and when I was president of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit D27/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want you, Mr. Lukic, please, to point out to the Trial Chamber where the street is and where your apartment is on that street, or was.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record -- just so the record is clear, you're pointing to -- you're not pointing to it yet.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. You're pointing to an area which is on the corner of another street. Is it Ulica Edvard Kardelj?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Djuro Djakovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Djuro Djakovic. And so the record is clear, the street you're pointing to is Ulica Ivo Lola Ribar, which is the street parallel to Ulica Marsala Tita.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You gave evidence yesterday that you were working fairly long hours during the period of 1992 and 1993. When you were working those long hours, how many times do you think -- or can you estimate how many times you would have stayed in your apartment after work, rather than going to the village?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the occasions when I stayed, I would spend the night in the apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over that period when you were working long hours, approximately how many times do you estimate that you stayed there after work?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 10 times a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By 1992, you'd been working for the municipality for some 10 or 11 years, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, since 1981.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were a fairly senior official by that stage, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was director of Internal Revenue Agency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a senior position, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, a senior position within the administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to clarify something from your evidence yesterday or the day before, when you -- following the elections in 1990, the multi-party elections, what were you doing between then and 19 -- April 1992? I just want you to tell us what your job was between then and 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was an official without a portfolio. I was an official that had not been assigned to any particular department. And I was pursuant to the law on state administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you actually doing as an official without a portfolio? What did your job involve?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I continued to work in the Internal Revenue Agency; however, I was not authorised to sign documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been authorised to sign documents before as the head of the internal revenue section?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all tax documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was this in effect a demotion for you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was removed from office, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The political party that you had supported, I think you said, had got three seats -- only three seats on the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You think it was a result -- or was it a result of your membership of that political party or support for that political party that you lost your position as the head of the Internal Revenue Agency?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after 10 years you'd reached the -- a senior position in the council. There was a change of government, and you were demoted for what you consider political reasons. Is that a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your -- I'm sorry. In effect, your career was going nowhere, while you maintained your membership with Ante Markovic's party; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that is calling for speculation, what would happen in future with his career. It's pure speculation what would happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness has already given evidence that as far as he was concerned he was demoted because of his association with the political party he was in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And I think it's -- the question can be answered by the witness. It's not so much speculation, considering the context in which the incident occurred regarding employment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pursuant to the law on state administration, officials without portfolio could keep that status for six months. And I cannot now say what would have happened had I not been re-elected Chief of the Internal Revenue Agency. Perhaps I would have been appointed director in some municipal enterprise. I don't know. However, I was not appointed to a position in the executive council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was at that stage when you were an official without a portfolio -- it was a fairly smart political move to switch to another party, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was appointed Chief of Internal Revenue Agency before I became a member of another political party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you lose your job, then?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that time there was something that the majority of the parties that held power in the municipal assembly decided upon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The three main parties were, of course, the HDZ, the SDA, and the SDS; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the -- and you're nodding to that.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the SDS support your retaining your position as head of the Internal Revenue Agency?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In November of 1992 -- no, I'm sorry, of 1990, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is this a suitable time, Your Honours? It's 3.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take our break now and continue our proceedings at 16.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic, you have an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I do apologise. My colleague -- just one clarification with regard to the issue which was raised by His Honour Judge Lindholm. In fact, yes, our internal number, document RH27, regarding the office time of the municipal organs was introduced in our bundle of documents in order to be introduced as an exhibit. But after verification, we found that under the RB4 is the same document with the same numbers and everything, and this document, RB4, was tendered into evidence and now it's D75/1. And I do apologise for this inconvenience, and I wish to thank Judge Lindholm for this instruction. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination continues.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise to the Trial Chamber, and to my learned colleague. We are not receiving the transcript on our laptops, none of these three laptops. So if someone from the technical booth could come. I mean, I don't want to interrupt the trial.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are aware of the problem. I've already requested a technician to verify what went wrong during the break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We can continue, since the screens are recording.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the break, when Mr. Pantelic was asking you questions, he asked you about songs you might have heard in the town, and your answer was you often heard songs coming from the TO headquarters building. And then you said, "After work hours, I lived in a village which was 11 kilometres away." Now, in light of your response to me just before the break, that you actually spent about 10 days a month after work living in -- staying at your apartment in town, do you want to amend your answer?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Occasionally I went home several times, but at least 10 days were spent in the apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said -- you said 10 days a month. Now, the reason I ask you -- I want to ask you that is in relation to the songs. You understand?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard the singing during the working day. My apartment is about 600 or 700 metres away from the TO headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To get to your apartment, you had to walk out into the street and walk very close, maybe 20 metres or so, from the TO building from where the songs were coming, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the songs, of course, were coming, I suggest, every night in the first -- in the first few months after April the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard the songs during work hours and not continuously, not during the whole day, only occasionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the songs, as you say "songs," not "song" included -- one called "From Topala to Ravna Gora," correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that song too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there's another one called, "General Draza's guards are standing all around."

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know the song or you don't remember hearing it, "General Draza's guards are standing all around"?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know the song.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can assist my colleague. This is one very same song. It starts -- it is actually the same song. It starts with from --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the words of that song, "from Topala to Ravna Gora."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how about this one: "Oi, Balija, we're going to slit your throats." Do you remember hearing that one?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Balija" is an offensive term to Muslims, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a derogatory name for Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about "Hello General Mihajlovic"? Is that a song you heard coming from the TO building?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which song this is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in your own words, apart from "From Topala to Ravna Gora," which includes the words "General Draza's guards are standing --"

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are all General Draza's, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what other Serb songs did you hear being sung from the TO building?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That song was sung most frequently. There was also the song, "Over Kraljevo." I can't remember, but they were old Serb songs from the old times. I don't know which ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "old times," are we talking World War II and the Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are Serb traditional songs. The Serbs sang those songs. I don't know when they were written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were -- they were nationalistic and patriotic Serb songs, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Patriotic songs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew at that point that non-Serb prisoners were being detained in the TO and SUP buildings, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was obvious to you that it was the prisoners who were singing these songs, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With the guards, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the prisoners weren't -- the prisoners were Muslim and Croat, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that -- yes, that was so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You wouldn't expect them to be singing Serb patriotic and nationalistic songs voluntarily, would you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It's a pure speculation. What the witness can say what the other persons would expect or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't see that question as asking for speculation. It's a proper question, and the Prosecution will continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was: You wouldn't expect Croat and Muslim prisoners to be voluntarily singing Serb patriotic and nationalistic songs, would you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you wouldn't expect that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that stage, in May -- April/May 1992, you'd risen to the position of being one of the top half dozen or so civilian officials in Bosanski Samac, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the end of May 1992, you were the vice-president of the executive council, which was working closely with the Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name half a dozen officials who were higher than you in Bosanski Samac by the end of May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was the director of the Internal Revenue Agency, and the vice-president of the executive council. Above me was the president of the executive council. As far as the executive council was concerned then there was the secretary or the chief of the MUP, the chief for National Defence, and naturally the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Council for the Prosecution, can you speak slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I will speak more slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So if it wasn't a half dozen, would you say that you were one of the top dozen civilian officials in Bosanski Samac by the end of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was among the higher officials but not among those six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said "dozen." I went up from a half dozen to a dozen. Would you agree you were in the top dozen?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't counting, but among the 15, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had some fairly significant powers yourself, including the authority to enter into contracts and legal relations for the municipality, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding the finances, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had the power to sign contracts and legal documents for the municipal authority, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the executive council, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also had a power of attorney, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's implied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the reasons you had these was because of your legal qualifications; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. It is not an objection. In 30 -- page 36, line 17, the question was: "You also had a power of attorney, didn't you?" Well, I received the translation that it was not actually precise word of "power of attorney" in English. So could my colleague can clarify, if the power of attorney was a document for certain action or certain sign or contract or whatever or it's something else, because the witness and all of us who are receiving B/C/S translation, it's something different that we got in our earphones. So maybe in a few details maybe my colleague can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution can clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Simply a power of attorney to act on behalf of the municipal -- sorry, the executive council and the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of finances.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And again, Your Honour, in this question we have two terms, "executive council" and "the municipal assembly." So I don't think -- what exactly my colleague means, whether it means executive council or municipal assembly. It's a two-folded question, I believe. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It comes from a document Mr. Pantelic provided the Prosecution with. It's sitting over there. He knows what it is. I'm not going to put it to the witness at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The executive council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your -- the situation in March 1992 for you was that you were an official without portfolio on the council -- sorry, the municipal assembly while simultaneously you had been elected to the executive council of the parallel municipal authority for the Serbian authority; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're thinking of the Assembly of the Serbian People.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The situation is that you were simultaneously working at the elected municipality as an official without portfolio, while at the same time you had been elected an executive member -- sorry, a member of the executive council of the Serbian Assembly of Bosanski Samac. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The membership in the municipality of the Serbian -- the Serbian municipality in the committee did not function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact is that you were elected and you were a member of the executive council at the same time that you were working -- sorry, the executive council of the Serbian parallel institution at the same time that you were working as a paid employee of the Bosanski Samac Municipal Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 6th of March, 1992 you attended a meeting with Colonel Nikolic from the JNA, Mr. Blagoje Simic, Mr. Dragan Lukac, Mr. Milos Bogdanovic in the police station, didn't you, in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was about -- if I could jog your memory, it was about roadblocks in Donja Crkvina. Does that assist your memory?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you attended that meeting, didn't you? The answer is yes?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what capacity did you attend the meeting of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, what's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. Could -- my learned friend can give the reference of the page number of the transcript with regard to this event, because I'm not so sure that --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It was the work of Colonel Nikolic or the other persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can continue cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were at the time an officer without portfolio, what was the reason why -- for what reason did you attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that the president of the executive council authorised me on behalf of the executive council as an official without portfolio to go to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also attended a meeting with General Mladic in the autumn of 1992 in the municipal building with Mr. Blagoje Simic, didn't you -- I'm sorry, Mr. Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And General Mladic came to the municipal building and stayed there for several hours with his bodyguards standing outside the door, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Spent about 40 minutes maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of the meeting with General Mladic in autumn 1992 in the offices of the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that I worked in the office and somebody came in and said, "General Mladic is in the municipal building." And I went outside and I saw the general, and then he entered my office. There was no invitation. He didn't give any reason, nor did he announce himself for this meeting. He was probably just passing through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said you spent 40 minutes speaking to General Mladic. What did General Mladic want to tell you? What did he say to you in this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked about the work obligation, about the functioning of the economy, how much the municipality was assisting the army. These were the main questions that he had, and I reported to him on all of these questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many other meetings did you have with General Mladic after that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff in 1992 took the place of the municipal assembly, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the municipal assembly wasn't meeting, so the Crisis Staff was performing all the functions of local government, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The municipal authorities or whatever the assembly is doing -- the assembly authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just an intervention to the transcript. The witness said not "the municipal authorities" but the "assembly authorities" in terms of what the scope is for the assembly. Otherwise municipal authorities is something larger and it does not reflect correctly what the witness said. So maybe my learned friend can clarify with that the witness, what was his explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In my submission speaks for itself. The witness said, "Yes, the municipal authorities or whatever the assembly is doing -- the assembly authorities." Meaning, I thought, that they were doing everything the municipal authorities or assembly was doing before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The answer seems to imply that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The municipal -- I withdraw that. The Crisis Staff had a very important role in life in Bosanski Samac in 1992 and 1993, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It substituted for the work of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It also liaised with the National Assembly and the national -- sorry, the Republika Srpska government, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Crisis Staff -- I withdraw that. One of the jobs of the Crisis Staff, or one of its roles, was to implement government policy, that is, Republika Srpska policy; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And government policy was communicated to the Crisis Staff and the executive board through a variety of means, such as national assembly decisions, government decrees, presidency decrees.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was very important for the Crisis Staff and the executive council to know what decisions the presidency and National Assembly were making in that period 1992/1993, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the executive board too, and I know about the Crisis Staff, but I wasn't in the Crisis Staff, so I can't give you a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The executive council was very concerned to know what the decisions -- sorry, what were the decisions -- sorry, to know of the decisions of the presidency and the National Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because it was your role to implement those on the ground, if you like, in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the National Assembly and the War Presidency -- the Presidency of the Republika Srpska communicated its decisions and policies by publishing them and sending them to local organisations such as the executive council and the Crisis Staff of Bosanski Samac; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They sent their regulations or laws through the Official Gazette, decrees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also received decrees before they had been published in the Official Gazette, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some. If we were in the government and the decision was already ready for publication, then somebody would be able to bring it back, so it was available to them earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Liaison between the Crisis Staff and the National Assembly was quite important in those times of war, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And each local Crisis Staff or Serbian assembly had representatives which it sent to the National Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll put it another way. Each Serbian local assembly in the SAOs had representatives nominated to go to -- to attend National Assembly meetings; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your own Serbian Assembly, Bosanski Samac, nominated Dr. Blagoje Simic and Mirko Dragic or appointed them as representatives to the Serbian People in the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's incorrect, is it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that Dr. Blagoje Simic and Mirko Dragic were not appointed representatives to the National Assembly from the Serbian municipality in which you resided?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained this yesterday. The National Assembly would always invite some of the representatives to monitor the work of the session in their capacity as observers. I don't know what National Assembly session you're talking about, but sometimes they attended a session of the National Assembly to monitor its work. But here we are talking only about one session and not a number of sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P124.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want you to turn to item 4. I don't know what page it is on in the B/C/S version. And a decision -- where it says, "Decision," the second one. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
