utterances.text: Do you agree now it's a decision of the 28th of March, 1992, number 1-3/92, saying, "Dr. Simic and Mirko Dragic are appointed representatives of the Serbian people from the territory of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation in the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what it states.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We're not receiving video evidence on our displays.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Because it wasn't on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: None of us, so -- something about it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Was it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now it's okay. Now it's okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I'm asking you: That is the official decision appointing them as representatives to the National Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But let me just tell you, the National Assembly had requested for the municipalities to send them the names of the people who would sometimes, from time to time, attend the National Assembly meetings as observers. And our municipality provided them with those names. When the National Assembly of Republika Srpska thinks it necessary to call to attend one of its sessions some of our -- some of the representatives from our municipalities, then they would come. But they were not permanent deputies to the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They may not have been permanent deputies, but they were entitled to attend as representatives; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon invitation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Simic was --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they received adequate accreditation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Simic was wounded in 1992, July 1992. Do you remember when Dr. Simic was shot?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that, but I don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was shot or wounded on the 24th of July, 1992. Has that helped jog your memory?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the president of the executive council I heard that he had been wounded, but I don't know the reasons. He never told me the details of his wounding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was in hospital until the 30th of July, that is, some five -- five or six days. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If he was in hospital, he wouldn't have been able to attend a National Assembly meeting held on the 25th of July, 1992, would he?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if he was in hospital, surely he was unable to attend. But it is also possible that he was never invited to attend this particular session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 25th of July, the War Presidency at a decision signed by -- decision number 177/ -- sorry -10/92 authorised Stevan Todorovic to attend the National Assembly meeting held on the 25th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that it would be fair for this witness if we are speaking about any of the documents which are tendered as exhibits to have a look on that and then to make a comment. Otherwise, if, you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Whatever, it's 177-10/92, who knows about that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. In fairness to the witness, since he has discussed so many document, perhaps the Prosecution would handle that part of questioning like that. Show him the document and then ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of course, I was actually going to, Your Honour. In case my friend is worried. Could the witness please be shown P113.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, if you'd be, my friend, so kind -- you said transcript 1577, but there are -- there is five digits in the transcript. Could you please be so kind to repeat because we are not able to find.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Page 1577, the 24th of September, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's impossible because -- 2001. Sorry. Because I thought that you were referring -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. You've seen the document that's in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that that's an authorisation of the War Presidency for Stevan Todorovic to attend -- sorry, to represent an act for Bosanski Samac at the National Assembly on the 25th of July, 1992 at a time when Dr. Blagoje Simic, who was the nominated representative was in hospital? Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that Dr. Blagoje Simic was invited. But instead of him, the War Presidency sent someone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The executive board or executive council was regulated by a decision on -- decision dated -- decision 30th of May, 1992, 139-10/92. You may have discussed it. And it's set out in some detail the rights, duties, and obligations of the municipal board. You know the document, don't you? It's P112, and you discussed it in evidence yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could be shown P112.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll take you to Article 1, the second paragraph, where it says, "The executive board shall report to the assembly, that is, to the Crisis Staff, on the situation in all aspects of social life, the implementation of policies, decisions and other regulations of the assembly, that is the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac."

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... of the executive board, that is to report on all aspects of social life, as written there; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of the competencies of the executive council. Social life is a rather white category.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm only reading back to you what it says in this document, which was signed by Dr. Simic on the 30th of May --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over the page it -- at Article 7, entitled, "Rights and obligations," it says, "When discharging its responsibilities set out in the constitution," that that of course is the constitution of Republika Srpska, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "And other regulations of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the executive boards have the right and duty to, one, monitor the situation of all the aspects of human activities and take measures to resolve issues related to those activities." That's what it says, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in accordance with the law on state administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The keywords are "all aspects of human activities and take measures to resolve issues related to those activities." It's written there in black and white, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your board had responsibilities for things such as welfare, didn't it, of the community?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, as far as social policy is concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Housing?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Employment?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Education?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Transport?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Economy, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Agricultural policies?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Public safety?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was basically your business to know what was happening in Bosanski Samac, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever falls within the competencies of the executive council, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was your business to know about the welfare of people in Bosanski Samac, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the centre for social work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was under your jurisdiction, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was the financial affairs that were under my jurisdiction, the budgetary matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the jurisdiction of the executive board or executive council.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes. In that case, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were quite wide ranging, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the decrees issued by the government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Welfare of the citizens of course includes Serbs, Croats, Muslims, and others, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1992, the schools were closed, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The schools actually started working in October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Between April and October 1992, the two -- the two school buildings were closed to school children, weren't they, in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The school year was finished on the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying you have a six-month school vacation in Bosanski Samac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It was on the 15th of April that the previous school year ended, and in October the government issued a decision in the beginning of the new school year in those municipalities where it was such that it could be organised, that the work of the schools could be organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two schools in Bosanski Samac, the elementary school and the high school or technical school, as you call it, could not be used between April and October 1992 because they were full of Muslim and Croat prisoners; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prisoners there were being detained without trial or charge, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. Because this was within the competencies of the police. The police had requisitioned these two facilities at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you were the vice-president of the executive board. You were a person with legal qualifications. You were on a board that was entrusted with monitoring all aspects of social life, including welfare in the municipality of Bosanski Samac. Are you seriously telling this Trial Chamber you don't know whether people were detained there without trial or charge?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not have information to that effect, so I couldn't give you a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The elementary -- the two schools were several hundred metres from your office and from your -- the place you stayed in several nights a week; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were aware that there were several hundred Muslim and Croat prisoners being held there; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you think they were being held there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had talked to the police commander, and in response to my question, he told me -- I wanted to know who those people were and why they were there. Anyway, he told me that they were being processed. What he meant was that there were indications that they had carried weapons or had been engaged in planning a rebellion, and it was to that effect that the police were conducting proceedings, their proceedings there. However, that was not within the competencies of the executive council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the vice-president of the executive council and a lawyer, did you ask him whether they were being -- whether they had been charged or were being lawfully detained?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said that an investigation was being conducted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document which I just referred to you and you have there refers to the constitution of the Republika Srpska. And as you know, unlawful deprivation of freedom is unlawful under the constitution which was in force at the time.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What steps did you take to find out as a person entrusted with the monitoring of all aspects of human activities in Bosanski Samac to find out whether or not these people were being lawfully detained?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That fell within the competencies of the public security centre, that is, the MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're basically saying you did nothing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not within the jurisdiction of the executive council. The public law and order is part of the competencies and the authority of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. It is only the MUP that can deal with it when it comes to the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you as a lawyer and vice-president of the executive council and a citizen have been concerned if hundreds of people were being detained without charge or trial and tortured or beaten in school buildings which were under the control of the Crisis Staff and your council?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I told the police chief, the police commander. I told him that I was concerned and that I would like to see this investigation to be completed as soon as possible. But as a member of the executive council, in that capacity; not as a person who had any kind of authority in that regard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever think to ask to inspect the facilities of the elementary school or the technical school for yourself?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Milan Simic, who was the president of the executive board, of course went there in his official capacity, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object to this question. First of all, this witness cannot know if Milan Simic -- well, maybe he does know, but first he needs -- our colleague has to ask him if he knows whether Milan Simic was going there or not going there. Then in what capacity, official or as a private person. This is a double-barreled question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The question is clear. The witness knew who Milan Simic was, and he can answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the persons who returned to Samac after 1996, having read the indictment, I heard and I realised that Milan Simic had been in these detention facilities, but I didn't know that and he didn't go there in his capacity of the president of the executive council, because he did not have any authority to that effect. But I did hear that he had visited these detention units with Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you hear that he had visited these facilities with Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1996 and 1997, from the persons who had returned to Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how Milan Simic as president of the executive board had access to the primary school in his official capacity?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that whenever he visited these detention facilities, he was accompanied by Stevan Todorovic. And according to what I heard from those who had returned, very often he was there -- actually, both of them were there in an inebriated state.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could Your Honours just excuse me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The situation was that before April the 16th, 1992 there was a democratically elected local government in Bosanski Samac, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the democratically-elected government was elected -- the first multi-party elections was in 1990 in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It resulted in three parties -- three main parties and some minor parties gaining seats in the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three main parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As of the 17th of April, 1992 that municipal assembly was no longer functioning, was it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that composition, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It wasn't functioning at all, was it, in any composition?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It wasn't functioning because it had been overthrown or taken over by Serb forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could not be convened because those deputies were no longer there. Part of them were no longer there. And then emergency state was declared and the assembly no longer functioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree, would you not, that the definition of a military coup d'etat is when the military takes over the government in a town, city, state, or country and replaces the elected government with one of its own, either civilian or military, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Theoretically, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the night of the 16th/17th of April, 1992, Serb paramilitaries in the JNA took over the town -- the municipality of Bosanski Samac, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't in Samac at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which soldiers were patrolling the streets on the 17th of April -- 17th and 18th of April, 1992 when you did reappear, Mr. Lukic? Were they Croatian soldiers, ABiH soldiers, or Serbian soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th of April, upon my return, there were soldiers of the Yugoslav People's Army patrolling there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is, of course, after Bosnia had been recognised as an independent state by the EU and the United States on the 6th and 7th of April, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was recognised then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course after a majority of the citizens of the country had voted for independence from Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a referendum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll take you back, then. On the 16th of April, a multi-party -- I'm sorry, the municipal assembly was comprised of a number of democratically elected representatives. On the 17th of assembly [sic] it was no longer existing and the streets were being patrolled by JNA soldier, you say. How do you say that the JNA soldiers had not taken over the town and replaced the democratically-elected municipal government with it own?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not claiming that they were not patrolling. On the 18th of April, I saw the soldiers of the JNA, and I didn't claim that they were not in town and not patrolling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not what I'm asking you, Mr. Lukic. On the 16th of April, there was a democratically-elected municipal assembly, which was controlling the municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, it was no longer in existence; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It had been replaced by the Serb Assembly of Bosanski Samac; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th of April, the Crisis Staff was declared, which means then there were Serbian authorities then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll put it that way. The 16th of April, democratically-elected government. 19th of April, Serb Crisis Staff. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In between, JNA soldiers, Serb paramilitaries, took over the town; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They controlled the town together with the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They didn't control the town on the 16th of April, when the democratically-elected assembly was in control, did they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- no, they didn't control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I put it to you again: What else could that be other than a forcible takeover or a local military coup d'etat?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is calling for a legal conclusion. Let's leave this to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That can't be a serious objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lazarevic. It's a question which the witness can answer, considering his level of operation and his level of education.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the question? The question was: What else could -- just let me finish it. The question was: What else could have happened other than a forcible takeover or a local military coup d'etat?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the reasons for what happened that day. That's why I can't tell you whether it was a forcible takeover or a non-forcible takeover. There had been information -- this is a military matter, and I'm not a military serviceman, so I can't give you an exact answer. But it is true that on the 18th, there were JNA troops in the streets. I saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There could be no reason for JNA troops to be in the streets at that point after the declaration of independence, could there? I withdraw that. There could be no -- I'll rephrase it. There could be no legitimate reasons for JNA troops to be in the streets controlling the town and vital facilities after Bosnia's recognition as an independent state by the EU and the US, for example, could there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The declaration of the state of emergency was a very, very serious step for the Crisis Staff to take, wasn't it, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what declaration you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the declaration of the state of emergency in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was a very, very serious step for the Crisis Staff to take in relation to control of the municipality, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The declaration -- the announcement -- just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just excuse me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A state of emergency could only be declared in very, very extreme circumstances, couldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And only as a result of a threat to the people of the municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... made upon very sound advice?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on a very firm assessment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if the assessment was wrong, the state of emergency should be revoked, shouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if the stated reasons for declaring the state of emergency turned out to be wrong, there would be no reason for the state of emergency to continue, would there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then the state of emergency should be terminated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it should be terminated immediately, shouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as there are no more reasons for it to exist any more, it is immediately terminated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if the reasons were wrong to start with for proclaiming it, it should never have been proclaimed in the first place -- one should never have been proclaimed in the first place. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The stated reasons for proclaiming the state of emergency in Bosanski Samac on the 19th of April, 1992 were, considering the difficult situation on the territory of the municipality --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Same suggestion, Your Honour. If we are speaking about a particular document, it would be fair for the witness to have the document in front of himself, not to have quotation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: P89. Could the witness please be shown P89.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll read it to you to save time while it's coming. The preamble says, "Considering the difficult situation on the territory of the municipality particularly in the town of Bosanski Samac where a paramilitary formation entered the municipality in order to carry --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down when reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Please, slow down. The interpreters have to follow you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Where a paramilitary formation entered the municipality in order to carry out an organised campaign of terror against the innocent population in the town and surrounding area, the Crisis Staff of Bosanski Samac municipality has made a decision on the introduction of a state of emergency on the territory of the municipality." Have you seen what I'm reading from?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could -- I do apologise. Could we have a B/C/S version on the ELMO because of our clients and also for the other members of the Defence team, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you read that, Mr. Lukic, the preamble?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, of course, the information was wrong. The state of emergency should never have been proclaimed, should it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the truth is that the only paramilitary formation which entered the municipality to carry out an organised campaign of terror was Serb paramilitary forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what it says here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that's not what says, but that's not what I'm saying to you. I'm saying that the only -- the truth is that the only paramilitary formation that ended the municipality in order to carry out an organised campaign of terror against the innocent population were in fact Serb paramilitary forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the Crisis Staff passed this decision, it was probably guided by some information it had at its disposal. I don't know. I wasn't present there, so I can't comment on this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first thing you did when you came back to work on the 18th of April was to go to the 2nd Posavina Command, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2nd Detachment, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 2nd Detachment. You went straight to the army when you came back to work, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to work, or I started to my office, and then I stopped by the 2nd Detachment to see what the situation was in town and to know where the president of the executive council and the entire executive council were, because my war assignment was in the executive council. So it was just by accident that I stopped by the 2nd Detachment, because it was on the way from my house to the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "executive council," are you referring to the Bosanski Samac Serb Municipality or the democratically-elected one?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My war assignment -- wartime assignment was in the executive council, and I meant the democratic one, the one that had been elected previously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you elected to the executive council of the democratic one -- the democratically-elected one?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of April, 1991, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With your legal qualifications, did you draft the decision on the introduction of a special wartime tax? I'm asking, were you one of the drafters of the decision on the special wartime tax?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was one of the participants, one of the authors of the draft.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown P102.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just while I'm on that issue of drafting, you, of course, had legal qualifications and had been working for the council for -- the assembly for some 10 years at that stage. Did you draft many documents of a legal type while working for the assembly?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the domain of the Internal Revenue Agency, yes, because I was Chief of Internal Revenue Agency, and I was authorised to propose drafts to the executive council and the municipal assembly only on that subject matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What about for the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac? Did you have a role in drafting legal-type documents for the assembly -- I'm sorry, for the municipality?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992 there was the Crisis Staff and the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what about for the War Presidency and the Crisis Staff? Did you assist by drafting legal-type documents, such as decisions, for the War Presidency and the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of finance, and the other topics were covered by other secretariats, Secretariat for Economy, for Health, Education, and Housing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said yesterday that it was the executive council which proposed the special wartime tax; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Crisis Staff, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you were working -- that's you, the executive council, was working fairly closely with the Crisis Staff at that time, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the domain of this subject matter, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The special wartime tax basically is drafted in relation to work obligation -- sorry, applies to work obligation and applies to the payment of tax, doesn't it? It's actually in two -- it's actually directed in two different things.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Special wartime tax was paid by those who worked abroad, meaning outside of the former Yugoslavia, and who did not respond to the general mobilisation call-up. The government of Republika Srpska gave a recommendation that a special wartime tax could be imposed on the salary of these individuals because prior to that salaries were taxed and the revenue thus collected went into the budget of the municipalities. A few months after that this revenue was redirected into the budget of the republic and the republic government, so the tax remained but it's end user was changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In line with the evidence you've given earlier, this, of course, applied to all peoples of all ethnicities, didn't it? Serb, Croat, Muslim, or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who came to Samac, because that was the only way we could collect these taxes, levy and collect. So all of those who came to Samac, those who lived and worked abroad, would pay this tax when they came back to Samac. The collection of this tax was conducted by the financial police at the border crossings at entry points into Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you're answering a completely different question to the one I asked. I asked you whether it was applied to people of all ethnicities. The answer is either yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But there were 99 per cent Serb there and 1 per cent of others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Article 2 says, "The taxpayer of the special wartime tax is an individual whose residence is on the territory of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac, et cetera, and who is currently on temporary employment abroad and in possession of valid work and residence permits, which were issued to him by the competent bodies of the country where he is staying." Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It applies on its face to people who have left the municipality but who were in residence there; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It applied only to those who came to Samac municipality and who were present in Samac municipality throughout the entire time. Those individuals who left the municipality did not pay wartime tax. Not a single such individual was expected to pay such tax, and we have records to prove this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I misreading, Mr. Lukic, am I misreading Article 2 where it says, "an individual whose residence is in Bosanski Samac currently on temporary employment abroad"? Am I misreading what it says there? Are those the words I'm reading from the paper?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But only -- or rather, if they left their residence, they were not subject to income tax. If they left the territory, they were not required to pay income tax.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we're obviously at cross-purposes here. I'm just quoting to you what the document says. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Article 2 says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it not clear that -- I think it's a question of language here. The witness is trying to say that those persons who had left the country, who didn't return each time they worked abroad and returned to Bosanski Samac. I'm sure it doesn't mean that people were commuting from the Balkans to other countries on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not -- I'm just taking the literal meaning of it, which says, "An individual whose residence is in Bosanski Samac and who is currently temporarily working abroad." That's all it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just asking him to agree that that's in fact what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the witness is explaining that those who had left --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- weren't subject to tax.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were not. That's exactly what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, is it perhaps -- Mr. Re has read out what the text says, so presumably for those persons who left the municipality of Bosanski Samac and, for example, stayed resident in Germany and never came back, even though the letter of the law would seem to apply to them, it would have been a question of not being able to enforce it. So it's a question of the enforceability of the legislation for those who never returned back to Bosanski Samac. Would that be correct do you think?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I may add, Your Honour, this is a matter of interpretation, so one is a literal approach and the other is the witness to try to explain how that was in reality. I mean, that's the basis of this discussion. So I think that my dear colleague shouldn't push this line strictly on the literary interpretation and leave the witness to broadly explain this issue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, thank you. But the witness just told us that he drafted the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But I think we have discussed it sufficiently, and he has answered what in practice how the law -- how that particular law worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. Lukic, should the person not pay the tax or fail to return, Article 3 says, in capital letters, "He will never be allowed to return to his country again and his entire movable property and real estate assets will be confiscated." That's what it says, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But that was never enforced. This was more of a psychological nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You drafted a document, a law -- a document with the status of law in Bosanski Samac saying that individuals who failed to return could have their entire movable property and real estate assets confiscated, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here. However, that was never enforced, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The answer is yes, that you drafted it; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The executive council did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of which you were the vice-president and presented it to the Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President of the Crisis Staff presented it -- the president of the executive council presented it to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, the people who had left Bosanski Samac at that point were Muslims and Croats, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this decision or this Article 3 could only have been pointed to -- directed towards Muslims and Croats who had left the territory; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you said that there were 99 per cent Serbs in town at that point; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The witness never said that. The witness said that the persons who paid this tax was 99 per cent Serbs, and he explained that the payment was on the border. So he didn't say that the population of Samac was 99 per cent of Serbs and the 1 the rest. So I kindly ask my dear colleague to keep --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will just check the transcript reference before I withdraw, if I may do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Please do check the transcript. I think the explanation by Mr. Pantelic appears to be what was in fact said by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I take Your Honours to -- and Mr. Pantelic, of course, to page 64, at line 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you're answering a completely different question to the one I asked. I asked you whether it was applied to people of all ethnicities. The answer is either yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But there were 99 per cent Serb there and 1 per cent of others.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The answer, in my submission, is fairly clear and is on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this applied to people who were temporarily working abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can't take it further. The answer -- there was an answer given, there were 99 per cent Serbs there, and I interpreted it in good faith that that was what he meant. If he means something and wants to tell us there was a smaller number of Serbs --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Another problem, Your Honour, we are suffering inconsistence with our notebook computers, laptop computers. We have only 33 pages. It's contrary to the official transcript on the display, which has 69. So we could -- we could not even find the page. So maybe in -- during the break the technical booth can help us. Because if I -- if I try to find page 64, it's impossible, because on my laptop I have only 33 pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's not working.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The same story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take our break and come back at 18.05.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I may, I wish to thank to our colleagues from the technical unit. Now all our computers are in order, and every one of us can follow the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's one thing. Another thing, I would like to reiterate that -- reading the page 64, where this issue was raised, it is not fair for the witness and it is not fair for the proceedings if our learned friend is taking out of context certain portions of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic, in fact, the Trial Chamber has decided that the witness will be given an opportunity to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because we want evidence to be correctly recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And to be understood by all parties, including the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So can the witness explain this tax and how it was implemented, to whom it applied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And as Judge Williams is telling me, the 99 per cent of the Serbs, because that's what is causing confusion. Was it of the people who were going abroad -- which may mean that the Croats and Muslims may not necessarily have left the territory but may not have been working abroad, or it could mean that they were not -- the Muslims and Croats had perhaps already left permanently, in which case their properties were subject to confiscation. So can you please explain this whole scenery about this tax, who paid it, what was happening on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, before he does, there was some confusion earlier when I was asking some questions about -- about the document, and I was talking about it being in two places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I talked about work obligations. The document is in two parts. Article 3 at the bottom refers to someone returning to carry out work obligations. The other part of the document refers to the payment of a wartime tax. That's what I was getting at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It was my -- I omitted to use the word -- to take the witness right to the words "work obligation," so there may be some confusion there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Because as I was saying, it's clearly directed to two things, one work obligation and, two, the tax. So maybe there should be some clarification on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness clarify.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must say that the wartime tax was paid by persons who were temporarily employed abroad. And "abroad" means countries outside of the former Yugoslavia. Who are these persons? They are persons who, while this decision was in effect, happened to come to town. How did they come? At the entry to Republika Srpska, the financial police, which was under the jurisdiction of the finance ministry, controlled or checked whether they had a receipt about paid income taxes, taxes on their salaries. After they come to the municipality, come to the town, they report in and then pay this tax. No one had their property confiscated ever, not any kind of property. And when I said that this applied to Serbs 99 per cent, what I meant was that during the war most of the people who came to the town or to the municipality were Serbs, and they were the ones who paid this duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what I was asking you before was Article 3 applies to a person failing to return in order to carry out his work obligation. I'm just reading what the document says, Article 3. The last words of Article 3 "or other competent body in order to carry out his work obligations." You see, it's about a person failing to return from abroad to perform a work obligation within 30 days. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government of Republika Srpska declared a general mobilisation, and it stated that those persons who were temporarily employed abroad or who are working in one of the western countries did not have to report to the general mobilisation call because then they would lose the status of workers in those countries or those companies, and that is why that is stated here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I'm asking you is: Reading this article, it is directed on its face, literally, at a person working abroad who fails to return within 30 days to carry out work obligations; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. That's what it states. But it applies to the persons that I mentioned earlier. This means that a man who is temporarily working abroad and does not wish to pay the wartime tax, then he had to come to the municipality and report and receive his military call-up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking for your interpretation --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was able to choose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please stop. I just asked you if that's what it said. If I wanted an interpretation, I'll ask you for it. And if I don't, I'm sure Mr. Pantelic will raise it.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Directed at people who don't return. The sanction is, and it's in capital letters is, "Confiscation of all property"; correct? That's what it says?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it states that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, in June 1992 most of the people who had left the territory of the Bosanski Samac were Croats and Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... residents of Bosanski Samac before they left, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And many Muslims and Croats left Bosanski Samac, leaving behind their property, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The work obligation published by the government and locally applied to all people regardless of ethnicity, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when Croat and Muslim people left the territory of Bosanski Samac, other people, mainly Serb, moved into their property, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the regulation on abandoned property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, there is nothing in this document which says it only applies to Serbs who have left Bosanski Samac, is there; yes or no? Just in the document. Yes or no? Do you mean no?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But let me explain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No explanation. I'm just asking you if there's anything in the document the answer is no. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not fair. I mean, it's -- finally, this is a legal document. I mean, we have to see what is the interpretation of it. What does it mean, yes or no? We cannot work with this -- maybe we can work with the facts. But if we're speaking about interpretation, it's not enough, yes or no, so I think the witness is entitled to explain that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. The Prosecutor have an explanation -- or if the Trial Chamber thinks it's necessary, the Trial Chamber will direct an explanation. But the sequence of questioning and answering is all right. If you want it explained, you can do that in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, at the time this was published, the Serbs, Croats, and Muslims were at war with each other in varying combinations, weren't they? The 15 of June, 1992 -- sorry, 13th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Republika Srpska of course was not recognised internationally or by the Muslims and Croats in the Federation; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. We have to know which period we are speaking about and --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just said the 13th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And by whom it was recognised.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just said the 13th of June, 1992. How much clearer can I be?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And another part is by whom it was recognised -- Bosnia was recognised. Because you firstly said it was European Union country and United States, and now what you're referring for? How many countries are recognised? So let's be specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think there was one at the time. It was Serbia. Although you could -- Republic of Yugoslavia. I think Mr. Pantelic knows that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you just ask the question again so that the witness can be clear and give us an answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Republika Srpska was recognised internationally by no other entity than Yugoslavia at that point; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There would be no reason for Muslims and Croats to return if they were abroad to answer a work obligation gazetted by the Republika Srpska during a time of war with their own people, would there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it didn't apply to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would be absurd to think that Muslims and Croats would return to answer a work obligation to fight against or to work against their own people, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many Muslims in town who lived there throughout the whole war. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about people returning from abroad, especially those who left perhaps as refugees. You would agree it would be absurd for them -- for the Republika Srpska to expect them to return to answer a work obligation, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't asked, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on its face, this document is directed at Muslims and Croats who have left Bosanski Samac and are unable to return, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving to the wartime -- the tax. Someone who fails to pay the tax in Article 11, again in capital letters, within the period stated, "Shall never be allowed to return to the territory of the municipality and all his movable property and real estate assets shall be confiscated." Do you see that? Article 11.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's your words and you drafted them; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was an added part of the text which was added when the final text was being adopted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also for psychological reasons?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. Because it was never implemented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On its face it is legalised exiling of people who have left the territory and haven't paid a wartime tax, isn't it, on its face?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision applies to people who worked abroad before the breakout -- the outbreak of hostilities, and this is what I've been trying to say the entire time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do the words -- what could the words "he shall never be allowed to return to the territory of the municipality" be other than legalised exiling of someone who has failed to pay a wartime tax? On its face, what could it be other than legalised exiling?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please speak slowly.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 3 states that within 30 days, they can return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, please speak slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If Your Honours pleases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about Article 11, Mr. Lukic. The words I read to you, please concentrate on those.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the answer yes, then? "Should a taxpayer fail to make regular tax payments following the expiration of the deadline stated in Article 9 - that's two months - of this decision, he shall never be allowed to return to the territory of the municipality and all his movable property and real estate assets shall be confiscated." I'll stop there. My question is the following: On the face of what is written there, this could only be -- the words "he shall never be allowed to return to the territory of the municipality" can only be seen as legalised exiling, what is written there.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it states. But if you read the whole decision, that is not the conclusion that you could draw from that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... decision, Mr. Lukic, and I'm asking you about Article 11. And we move on, "And all his movable property --"

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "And real estate assets shall be confiscated." On its face as written it can only be legalised confiscation without compensation of a person's entire property for failing to pay a wartime tax"; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it say, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a hand in the drafting of the statute of the municipality of the -- sorry, the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear what the witness said; yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He said no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you -- I withdraw that. You gave evidence earlier to Mr. Pantelic in relation to the massacre at Crkvina. I think your evidence was that you heard about it the next day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would have heard that Crni was one of the perpetrators, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Lugar, according to the information that I have, according to what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Excuse me for one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The work of the Crisis Staffs was regulated by the government of the Republika Srpska, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P128. And I'll continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were aware when you became the vice-president of the executive council that hundreds of people were being detained in facilities in Bosanski Samac, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that. I had heard about that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I ask counsel to provide the witness the B/C/S version as I seem not to have it on me at the moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think Mr. Pantelic showed you that document yesterday or the day before, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's an order of the prime minister dated the 26th of April, 1992, Prime Minister Branko Djeric, setting out the instructions for the work of the Municipal Crisis Staffs. I just want you to look at Article 3, where it says, "The Crisis Staff coordinates the function of authorities in order to ensure the defence of the territories, the safety of the population and property, the establishment of government and the organisation of all other areas of life and work. In so doing, the Crisis Staff provides the conditions for the municipal executive committee to exercise legal executive authority from the economy and other areas of life." Now, that sets out at the highest level of the Republika Srpska what the Crisis Staffs were supposed to be doing; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it establishes also the relationship between executive committees such as yours and the Crisis Staff, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you turn to paragraph 10, please, which says, "The non-fighting population and the wounded must be treated in the most humane fashion and in accordance with the ICRC. Prisoners of war also must be treated humanely and in accordance with the laws of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." The question I want to ask you is: What did the Crisis Staff, executive committee, the board of which you were a member, do to ensure that the non-fighting population and the wounded were treated in the most humane fashion and in accordance with the ICRC in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The executive council based its activity on the work of the economy, on the way the economy functioned. And I explained this two days ago. But I cannot give you any comment as to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 13: "War profiteers, gangs of looters, and similar shall be arrested and delivered to the investigating judicial organs of the Serbian Republic." My question is: What did the Crisis Staff or the executive committee, of which you were a member, do to ensure that war profiteers, gangs of looters, and similar were arrested and delivered to investigating judicial organs?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The supplies to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question I asked you is: What did the Crisis Staff or your committee do to ensure the arrest of looters, war profiteers, and similar?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The executive council adopted several decisions, that is, made proposals for several decisions to be adopted from this area of work. And I discussed them yesterday and the day before. These decisions were in accordance of the government decrees, and I cannot give you any comment on the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer is nothing that you know of; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The executive council did undertake steps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, if the executive council did, what were the steps that the executive council undertook to ensure the arrest and delivery to investigating judicial organs of war profiteers, gangs of looters, and similar?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not in the jurisdiction of the executive council. The executive council could not take any of those measures. They couldn't arrest people or prevent any such behaviour. This was in the jurisdiction of someone else. The executive council was simply an executive body, but only insofar as the economy and social work is concerned. It was not involved in all problems pertaining to the area of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you said the executive council did undertake steps. What did you mean when you said "did undertake steps"?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We issued an order whereby companies who were buying cattle were ordered not to buy the cattle in respect of which there were no adequate papers and ownership records.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your evidence has been to the effect that you don't encourage or condone discrimination -- ethnic discrimination; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't favour ethnic discrimination.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One ethnic group taking over the municipality -- taking over the organs of government could be -- I'm sorry. I withdraw that. One ethnic group taking over a municipal government for itself would discriminate -- I'll start again. The question I want to ask you is in relation to one ethnic group taking over a municipality. It would be discriminatory, would it not, for one ethnic group to take over the organs of government and not allow other ethnic groups to participate in the government, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This is a highly hypothetic and speculative question. Maybe my learned friend can go directly. Do you think that the Serbs from Samac in 1992 -- what does it mean? I mean, otherwise we are in theory, in the level of theory. It does not help the proceedings here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic, you won't direct the Prosecution how to cross-examine. The Prosecution is in order. They can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would be discriminatory, would it not, for one ethnic group to take over the organs of government and not allow other ethnic groups to participate in the government; wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would not be something that you would participate in; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not involved in personnel policy, but no, probably not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P124.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We already know that on the 28th of March, 1992 you were elected a member of the executive council of the Serbian Municipality -- Serbian Assembly of Bosanski Samac. We already know that. It's in evidence here. I want you to turn to Article 5 of the constitution -- I'm sorry, of the decision to establish an Assembly of the Serbian People. That's the first decision inside the document. Article 5, "The assembly of the Serbian People of Bosanski Samac, et cetera, shall consist of the deputies of the Serbian Democratic Party of Bosanski Samac, Gradacac, Orasje, and Odzak. Other deputies of Serbian ethnicity shall also become deputies of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo upon signing a statement of secession to the assembly." Have you read that? Now, that, of course, was the statute of the -- or that, of course, related to the body which took over government in Bosanski Samac, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at this moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was published in the gazette on the 3rd of June, 1994, year 1, number 1.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is probably a mistake. I don't know how this could be published in 1994, because the decision dates back in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, whatever -- whatever its publication date, this article only allows for, "Deputies of the Serbian Democratic Party and other deputies of Serbian ethnicity to participate -- or sorry, to become deputies of the assembly, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document does not contemplate Muslims, Croats, or people of other ethnicities to become deputies of the Serbian assembly, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, this was the assembly which was in power in the town -- sorry, in the municipality after the takeover, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the assembly that was held in December 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was also the assembly that was held in December -- I withdraw that. 1992. So in 1992, the assembly did not allow non-Serbs to participate in it, did it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision. In the course of 1992, until the 17th of April, there was only one assembly which was official. That was the multi-ethnic assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just referred to an assembly in December 1992. That assembly was held as a result of this decision, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that -- this decision does not allow non-Serbs to participate as deputies in the assembly, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is a discriminatory document, isn't it? It discriminates against non-Serbs on its terms, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Article 9 of that decision, it says, "Distribution of assets and liabilities and the takeover of public -- sorry, of property, public books, and other documentation shall be carried out via mixed commissions, composed of representatives of the municipality of the Serbian People and representatives of existing assemblies." That's what it says, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this article is directed at the Serbian Assembly of Bosanski Samac taking over the assets, liabilities, public property books, and documentation of the existing democratically-elected municipality -- Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if a division of assets and liabilities takes place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, of course the existing democratically-elected Assembly of -- Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac wasn't consulted before this decision was made in Article 9, was it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not participate in its work, but probably not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown P71.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, Mr. Lukic, handed over -- I withdraw. Mr. Lukic, you are aware, are you not, of the numbering of Crisis Staff decisions, weren't you? Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to the number?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at me, not the document. You are aware, are you not, of the numbering order of Crisis Staff documents, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They had a protocol of their own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your work, working with the Crisis Staff, you were aware of the numbering of their decisions sequentially, just like the executive committee did, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One, two, three, four, five, six, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document you have in front of you is number 95-10/92, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1998 -- I'm sorry, in December 1996 Tribunal investigators visited you in your office in Bosanski Samac in relation to documents, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told them -- you told them that you had some documents but some were with someone's counsel in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember saying that, that some of the documents were with someone's counsel. I remember that the investigators were there and that I had given them all of the documents that were at my disposal. Ms. Nancy visited me and Ms. Maria Velinkonja [phoen] as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And in April 1998, Mr. Pisarevic handed over a large number of documents which you had produced or you had found relating to the Crisis Staff and the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave documents only to Ms. Nancy and Ms. Maria.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honours. I don't know where this comes from, what my colleague is saying, that I received documents from Mr. Lukic and the documents that he had from some other sources. No, we never received any document from Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can't take that any further. If that's -- if I'm wrong about that, I withdraw it and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I was just wondering about counsel giving evidence on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It was information I was given. It may be incorrect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You signed a receipt on the 11th of June, 1998 for the receipt of several hundred Crisis Staff documents.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those documents you handed over Crisis Staff documents --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed this for whom?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the Tribunal. It acknowledged the receipt of --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a handwritten --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... several hundred documents. The document in front of you, P71, wasn't one of those, was it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO LUKIC [Resumed]
